arXiv_CondMat.summary: Topological Deep Learning (TDL) is designed to learn features associated not only with nodes but also with edges, triangles and higher dimensional simplices. However, most TDL approaches, being based on boundary operators and Hodge Laplacians, have the limitation that features and signals cannot be lifted or lowered across more than one dimension per layer. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we propose the adoption of the cup and cap products. Specifically, we formulate the Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network (CCNN), a topological deep learning architecture designed to learn node-based variables (or 0-cochains) by taking into account their many-body interactions (e.g. triangles) present in the data. We validate CCNN by assessing its performance on the TopoBench datasets, demonstrating its competitive performance with respect to other simplicial complex neural networks.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We show that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph, generalizing the previously developed graph-theoretic framework for Markov networks. These representations yield asymptotic results, including the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting, where non-Markovian corrections appear in higher moments. For finite-mean sojourn times, the framework recovers the known stationary distribution through a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem, with transition rates replaced by pseudo-rates. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short graph-theoretic proof of the previously established constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to extend established results on weak ergodicity breaking for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks, allowing for generally heterogeneous, transition-dependent waiting-time distributions.

arXiv_CondMat.title: The Puzzle of the Replica Transition at Ising Criticality
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Critical quantum ground states exhibit universal properties governed by conformal field theories (CFTs), yet some of these universal signatures remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising chain in 1+1d at its quantum critical point. In particular, numerical studies have long identified universal contributions to its ground-state measurement statistics, but their origin remains unexplained. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement statistics, with the replica limit $Q\to 1$ describing the physical Born-averaged ensemble. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit $Q \to 1$, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal O(1) constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Microscopic Connection between Phonon Hall Viscosity and Acoustic Faraday Effect in Spin-Orbit-Coupled Magnets
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The acoustic Faraday effect probes phonon Hall viscosity through the rotation of transverse acoustic polarization, conventionally interpreted in terms of circular birefringence. We show that magnetic order breaking rotational symmetry generates anisotropic phonon responses and elliptically polarized eigenmodes, so that Faraday rotation cannot be attributed to Hall viscosity alone. To elucidate their microscopic origin and consequences, we derive spin-strain couplings from a generic spin-orbit-coupled exchange model. We identify transverse strain couplings for propagation along the c-axis arising linearly from the changes in the bond-dependent interactions, along with strain-induced g-tensor contributions. Applying our theory to $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, we find that static strain responses modify the extraction of Hall viscosity from Faraday rotation, yielding a value significantly different from that inferred assuming rotational symmetry. Our results establish a microscopic connection between magnetic interaction, lattice dynamics, and phonon Hall viscosity in spin-orbit-coupled magnets.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Hereditary Effective Atom Theory for Large-Scale Atomic Structure Prediction
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Predicting the atomic structure of large systems requires simultaneous exploration of atomic positions, species, and, generally, the number of atoms. The combinatorial growth of possible arrangements can make this search difficult even for standard global optimization methods. We introduce Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), which integrates Effective Atom Theory (EAT) into a genetic algorithm. HEAT combines EAT's continuous relaxation of atomic positions, species, and population with the global search capabilities of genetic algorithms. Central to the method is a crossover scheme that directly superimposes two parent structures and relaxes the combined structure. HEAT outperforms conventional genetic-algorithm baselines in recovering a missing 240-atom H sublattice, predicting a 364-atom edge-dislocation core, and reconstructing a 1150-atom interior region of twisted-bilayer $\mathrm{WSe_2}$ from experimental ptychographic constraints. These results demonstrate how continuous effective-atom relaxation improves the exploration of large combinatorial structure spaces.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Layer-Parity Control of the Superconducting Diode Effect in Monolayer NbSe$_2$
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The superconducting diode effect is often associated with finite-momentum pairing, although model studies indicate that rectification reflects the asymmetry of the free energy about its minimum rather than the equilibrium pair momentum itself. Using a Wannier-based, self-consistent finite-$\mathbf Q$ Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach with a Fermi-surface-adaptive quadrature that converges the critical currents, we show that the layer parity and orientation of magnetic proximity select the diode response of monolayer NbSe$_2$. For in-plane exchange, the equilibrium pair momentum $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ and the diode efficiency are both linear in the layer-odd exchange contrast: parallel proximity on the two Se sublayers is reciprocal, and antiparallel proximity doubles the response. An out-of-plane component separates the two observables. It leaves $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ nearly unchanged but, through pair breaking, suppresses the efficiency by more than an order of magnitude and, at low temperature, reverses it. Purely out-of-plane exchange, for which $C_3$ symmetry forbids a helical term, keeps $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}=0$ yet produces a trigonal diode effect, controlled by the layer-even exchange and larger than the in-plane one above $0.65$~meV at $0.58$~K. Magnetic layer parity thus selects between a helical and a trigonal diode channel. This trigonal channel provides a candidate intrinsic contribution to the field-free rectification reported in NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$. The model predicts that two-sided out-of-plane proximity cancels it when antiparallel and, at the same exchange per layer, enhances it about fourfold when parallel, in the computed range.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Chiral superconductivity on a closed Klein bottle: a chirality wall and its Majorana seam spectrum
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We study a spinless $\pi$-flux lattice superconductor whose normal-state momentum-space fundamental domain is a Klein bottle. Within this model, a glide lift and a hidden antiunitary symmetry independently force the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) Chern number to vanish. A diagonal pairing breaks the antiunitary obstruction exactly when its real part is nonzero; this is necessary, not sufficient, for a chiral phase. We derive explicit Pfaffians determining Chern parity and identify three analytic families of gap closings in a real-pairing section. For a chiral state on a closed real-space Klein bottle, the prescribed pairing and gluing produce a $\Delta C=2$ chirality wall. A translation-invariant unfolding resolves two co-propagating Majorana branches. Their finite-size levels depend on circumference and holonomy; the near-zero pair is lifted at first order by allowed local seam perturbations. A cut-cylinder control has the same low-energy channel count, so gluing reconnects existing gapless content. We also distinguish literal gluing from deck projection: particle--hole symmetry exchanges the deck eigenblocks, precluding their interpretation as independent BdG quotient Hamiltonians. Finite odd-frequency correlations track holonomy and local splitting, while cylinder and ordinary-wall controls show that their presence is not specific to Klein gluing. The contribution is a model-specific account of pairing compatibility, closed-surface seam spectra and finite correlations. The energy cost is evaluated for a fixed pairing background; neither a protected zero mode nor a self-consistent wall solution is claimed.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Whether carbon forms crystalline structures beyond diamond at terapascal pressures remains unresolved. Predicted for nearly four decades, the denser BC8 phase has lacked direct crystallographic evidence. Here we report the first direct crystallographic identification of BC8 carbon, formed as a single crystal from molten carbon during laser-driven decaying-shock compression of [100]-oriented diamond following loading above 1.1 TPa. Using in situ orientation-resolved single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we observe discrete Bragg spots whose spacings and angular relationships are reproduced by a common orientation matrix within each indexed BC8 reflection group, providing constraints beyond powder peak matching. Our single-crystal formation strategy and direct diffraction evidence resolve the decades-long quest for a post-diamond carbon structure, demonstrating how dynamic loading pathways can make predicted high-pressure phases experimentally accessible.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Principles of Quantum Communication Theory: A Modern Approach
arXiv_CondMat.summary: This is a preliminary version of a book in progress on the theory of quantum communication. We adopt an information-theoretic perspective throughout and give a comprehensive account of fundamental results in quantum communication theory from the past decade (and earlier), with an emphasis on the modern one-shot-to-asymptotic approach that underlies much of today's state-of-the-art research in this field. In Part I, we cover mathematical preliminaries and provide a detailed study of quantum mechanics from an information-theoretic perspective. We also provide an extensive and thorough review of quantum entropies, and we devote an entire chapter to the study of entanglement measures. Equipped with these essential tools, in Part II we study classical communication (with and without entanglement assistance), entanglement distillation, quantum communication, secret key distillation, and private communication. In Part III, we cover the latest developments in feedback-assisted communication tasks, such as quantum and classical feedback-assisted communication, LOCC-assisted quantum communication, and secret key agreement.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, and Gauge Fields
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Key to solving many societally-relevant problems in materials science, quantum chemistry and nuclear physics is understanding their fundamental microscopic quantum behaviour. All of these problems can be phrased as fermionic (e.g. electrons) and bosonic particles (e.g. lattice vibrations, photons) interacting with each other. However, solving these systems of strongly-interacting fermions and bosons is out of reach for classical computers and also non-error-corrected qubit-only quantum computers. In this paper, we introduce a hybrid qubit and bosonic-oscillator quantum-simulation framework, which is so efficient that it could simulate some of these strongly-correlated problems even without error correction. Specifically, we leverage the available universal bosonic gate set with O(1) operations per gate as a function of the bosonic cutoff. This enables our framework to provide exact decompositions of higher-order fermion-boson interactions, including notoriously challenging terms such as (2+1)D gauge theories. We show how to compile dynamics, ancilla-free partial error detection, non-local observable measurement, and ground state energy estimation using both qubit-boson variational quantum eigensolvers and quantum signal processing. We introduce a "post-qubit quantum advantage" experiment which is both out of reach of near-term qubit-only quantum computers and classical computers. We develop a new qubit-based algorithm for simulating a beamsplitter which scales as almost-linear with boson number cutoff Nmax, asymptotically outperforming previously-known qubit methods. Our framework can be used in superconducting, as well as trapped-ion and neutral-atom hardware. This work establishes digital hybrid qubit-boson quantum simulation as a promising and advantageous method for solving the many challenging strongly correlated fermion-boson models of relevance to science and technology.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Why financial prices exhibit Brownian motion despite predictable order flow: An exactly solvable nonlinear price impact model
arXiv_CondMat.summary: In econophysics, there are two enigmatic empirical laws of financial market microstructure: (i) the market-order flow has predictable persistence due to metaorder splitting by institutional investors, as formulated by the Lillo--Mike--Farmer model. However, this phenomenon seems paradoxical given the diffusive and unpredictable price dynamics. (ii) The price impact $I(Q_{\rm tot})$ of a large metaorder $Q_{\rm tot}$ follows the square-root law, $I(Q_{\rm tot})\propto \sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}$. In this Letter, we reveal why price dynamics follows Brownian motion despite predictable order flow by unifying these enigmas via an exactly solvable model. We generalize the Lillo--Mike--Farmer model to nonlinear price-impact dynamics, which is mapped to a solvable L\'evy-walk model. Our exact solution shows that the price dynamics remains diffusive under the square-root law, even under persistent order flow, reflecting the finite variance of metaorder impact; our model is thus a minimal representative of the universality class of nonlinear price-impact models with finite-variance metaorder impact. This work illustrates the crucial role of the square-root law in mitigating price movements by large metaorders, leading to Brownian price dynamics, consistent with the efficient market hypothesis over long timescales.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Observation of hysteresis in an isolated quantum system of disordered Heisenberg spins
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We find energy-dependent hysteresis in an isolated Heisenberg quantum spin system, similar to thermomagnetic hysteresis in canonical spin glasses in contact with a thermal reservoir. Analogous to zero-field cooling and field cooling in conventional magnetic materials, an annealing protocol is devised to control the energy in an isolated system. Depending on the strength of disorder, the susceptibilities at zero field bifurcate at a specific energy, which signals the presence of different magnetic regimes. This behavior is apparent both in a numerical simulation by exact diagonalization of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian with twelve particles, as well as in an experiment with thousands of Rydberg atoms representing dipolar interacting quantum spins. The annealing protocols open a new path to explore the energy-dependent phase structure of spin systems at low energies. Our observation of a nonthermal metastable regime might indicate the existence of a phase transition to a novel state of isolated quantum spins.

arXiv_CondMat.title: HomID : Benchmarking Intrinsic Dimension Estimators on Homogenous Manifolds with Anisotropic Embeddings
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The manifold hypothesis suggests that data lies on manifolds with smaller intrinsic dimension (ID) than their ambient dimension. However there is no empirical agreement on the estimates for ID from different estimators for realistic datasets. Thus it is important to test ID estimators (IDEs) with targeted stressors. In this work, we consider the role of anisotropy. To this end, we propose HomID, a collection of homogeneous spaces with anisotropic embedding, for benchmarking ID estimators. We observe that methods that perform well on standard benchmarks systematically degrade on HomID under identical resource allocation. We further observe that anisotropic distortion of such benchmarks also results in performance degradation. Finally, we demonstrate that controlled anisotropic distortions induce systematic shifts in the distributions on which these methods rely, providing a concrete mechanism for the resulting estimation errors in two particular IDEs. The code for the project is available at https://github.com/a-writes-code/homid

arXiv_CondMat.title: Spectral Thresholds in Correlated Spiked Models and Fundamental Limits of Partial Least Squares
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We provide a rigorous random matrix theory analysis of spiked cross-covariance models where the signals across two high-dimensional data channels are partially aligned. These models are motivated by multi-modal learning and form the standard generative setting underlying Partial Least Squares (PLS), a widely used yet theoretically underdeveloped method. We show that the leading singular values of the sample cross-covariance matrix undergo a Baik-Ben Arous-Peche (BBP)-type phase transition, and we characterize the precise thresholds for the emergence of informative components. Our results yield the first sharp asymptotic description of the signal recovery capabilities of PLS in this setting, revealing a fundamental performance gap between PLS and the Bayes-optimal estimator. In particular, we identify the SNR and correlation regimes where PLS fails to recover any signal, despite detectability being possible in principle. These findings clarify the theoretical limits of PLS and provide guidance for the design of reliable multi-modal inference methods in high dimensions.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Statistical properties of quantum jumps between macroscopic states of light: reading an operational coherence record
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We propose an experimental apparatus to reveal the quantum coherence manifested in downward quantum jumps of amplitude bistability. The underlying coherent superposition of macroscopic quantum states is translated into the statistical properties of the integrated charge deposited in the detector circuit of a mode-matched heterodyne/homodyne detection scheme. At first, the dynamical evolution of a signal transmitted from an auxiliary cavity is employed to pinpoint a macroscopic switching event in a bistable main cavity subject to direct photodetection. Once the decision is made on the occurrence of a downward switch, the main cavity mode is let to freely decay to the vacuum, monitored to the production of an integrated charge. In the long-time limit, the charge distribution over an identical collection of pure states generated during the jumps converges to the Q function (heterodyne detection) or marginals of the Wigner function (homodyne detection) dictated by the phase of the local oscillator. When fluctuations over the ensemble step in, we connect the statistical properties of several switching events and the ensuing production of current records, to the cavity field correlations associated with the breakdown of photon blockade.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Fractional Quantum Hall States: Infinite Matrix Product Representation and its Implications
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We present a novel matrix product representation of the Laughlin and related fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions based on a rigorous version of the correlators of a chiral quantum field theory. This representation enables the quantitative control of the coefficients of the Laughlin wavefunction times an arbitrary monomial symmetric polynomial when expanded in a Slater determinant or permanent basis. It renders the properties, such as factorization and the renewal structure, inherent in such fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions transparent. We prove bounds on the correlators of the chiral quantum field theory and utilize this representation to demonstrate the exponential decay of connected correlations and a gap in the entanglement spectrum on a thin cylinder.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Generating entangled polaritonic condensates by pumping with entangled pairs of photons
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We investigate the steady state of two single-mode, uniform, spatially separated polaritonic condensates exposed to resonant pumping with entangled pairs of photons in the presence of incoherent exciton reservoirs created by nonresonant optical pumping. We demonstrate the principal possibility of driving the system to an entangled state despite its exposure to noises arising from the excitonic reservoirs and photon leakage through the microcavity mirrors. We estimate the minimum pair-induced polariton influx required to drive the system into a steady state that violates the partial-transpose criterion for entanglement. Furthermore, we trace the evolution of the system after a sudden switch-off of the entangled pumping. Our analysis provides estimates for the entanglement lifetime in a system of two exciton-polariton condensates.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Parisi formula and large deviations for mean-field spin glasses with Mattis interactions
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We consider convex mean-field vector spin glasses perturbed by a general Mattis interaction $N G(m_N)$, where $m_N$ is a bounded vector-valued empirical average and $G$ is continuous. We prove a Parisi-type variational formula for the limiting quenched free energy and a quenched large deviation principle for $m_N$, both at every temperature. The approach is simple and modular: the only model-specific spin-glass input is the variational formula for every linear tilt of $m_N$ together with differentiability of the resulting free energy. The classical G\"artner--Ellis, Varadhan, and Bryc transfers then treat an arbitrary continuous $G$. Thus the same argument applies to a broad class of empirical observables and Mattis potentials, without a separate constrained-free-energy calculation for each model. As a scalar specialization, the framework contains the Gaussian spin-glass surrogate used in mismatched rank-one matrix estimation.

arXiv_CondMat.title: High-temperature free energy for non-convex mean-field spin glasses with Mattis interactions
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We study enriched mean-field vector spin glasses whose covariance function need not be convex. In a quantitative short-time regime, corresponding to sufficiently high temperature in the usual physical parameterization, we prove convergence of the quenched free energy to the differentiable solution of a infinite-dimensional Hamilton--Jacobi equation proposed for non-convex models. We identify that solution through its characteristics and a unique fixed point. The argument does not assume replica symmetry. We then allow a general continuous Mattis interaction $N G(m_N)$, obtain the corresponding variational formula, and prove a quenched large deviation principle for $m_N$. As an explicit application, we treat a bipartite model with Mattis fields, which is closely related to the Restricted Boltzmann Machine. The application requires neither a replica-symmetry assumption nor ellipticity or Nishimori identities; its restriction is the same quantitative high-temperature condition as in the general theorem.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Everything at Every Scale: Scale-Invariant Diffusion with Continuous Super-Resolution
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Creating images from noise is image generation; reconstructing fine details from coarse inputs is super-resolution. Despite their practical differences, both can be understood as reversing information loss across scales. We introduce $\textbf{SKILD}$, a $\textbf{S}$cale-invariant $\textbf{K}$-Space $\textbf{I}$mage $\textbf{L}$earning $\textbf{D}$iffusion model that unifies generation and continuous super-resolution within a single unconditional framework. Both natural images and critical physical systems exhibit scale invariance, and we leverage it to design a forward process that attenuates image content from fine to coarse scales while injecting spectrum-matched Gaussian noise, making scale an explicit coordinate of the diffusion dynamics. The same trained reverse process performs generation and continuous super-resolution by varying only the starting timestep: $\textit{no task-specific architecture, no conditioning branch, no classifier-free guidance, no retraining per scale factor}$. Empirically, SKILD reaches FID $2.61$ and Inception Score $9.65$ on unconditional CIFAR-10, performs $2\times$--$8\times$ super-resolution on ImageNet from a single unconditional checkpoint while outperforming conditional models across perceptual metrics, and reconstructs critical Ising models whose connected four-point correlations closely track the ground truth.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Entanglement in Presence of Topological Interfaces and Dualities
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Entanglement through interfaces has attracted considerable attention in 2d conformal field theory (CFT). However, it is known that field-theoretic predictions based on the existing framework are in general incompatible with numerical results [1-4]. A new framework for entanglement through topological defects was recently proposed in [5]. It provides a general description of entanglement through topological defects and successfully reproduces the numerical results for the Ising model in all tested cases and regimes. The key insight is that the relevant quantum correlations are encoded in twisted states, allowing for the construction of the full reduced density matrix (RDM). In this work we pursue two objectives. First, we provide new examples by studying defects in the free boson CFT. Second, we extend the framework to topological interfaces connecting two, possibly distinct, CFTs. Of particular interest are interfaces relating dual theories. We show that the reduced density matrix for a duality interface is the projection of the vacuum reduced density matrix onto a single symmetry sector, closely paralleling the framework of symmetry resolution. Unlike symmetry resolution, however, the projection is imposed by the physical interface itself, demonstrating that duality interfaces reflect quantum correlations back into the entangling interval. We establish this mechanism for diagonal and non-diagonal rational CFTs as well as the free boson CFT. Relative entropy allows us to quantify the distinguishability of the duality interface RDM from the vacuum RDM.

arXiv_CondMat.title: GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We implemented on GPU a mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics simulation based on a momentum-jump-free theory. The trajectory spawning that was previously implemented on CPU for sampling enhancement was eliminated to avoid the overhead of thread divergence and dynamic memory allocation on the GPU. The method was applied to a three-dimensional spin-boson model and a three-mode model of $S_2 \to S_1$ internal conversion in pyrazine involving a conical intersection. A speedup of an order of magnitude compared to the CPU computation with spawning was achieved, as well as a linear scaling with respect to the number of sampling trajectories.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Lee-Yang theorem for fermions
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Lee-Yang theorems are a powerful tool for studying many-body systems, with applications ranging from analyzing phase transitions to proving the efficiency of certain classical and quantum algorithms. In this work, we prove a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem for the partition function of a broad class of interacting fermion models, implying the existence of a provably efficient quantum algorithm for estimating their ground-state energies. This class includes several well-known models such as the attractive Hubbard model, repulsive Hubbard model on bipartite graphs, and the interacting Hofstadter model. Our results also rigorously establish the nonexistence of phase transitions in these models in the presence of a nonzero local external field.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Dissipation accelerates quantum and classical simulation of open-system dynamics
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Simulating open quantum systems reveals how environmental coupling shapes relaxation, excitation transport, and the dynamics of quantum correlations. On quantum hardware, dissipative channels add operations and might seem to increase cost. However, we show that a broad class of Pauli noise, including depolarization, can ease quantum and classical simulation by exponentially suppressing high-weight components of Heisenberg-evolved observables. For bounded-degree Lindblad dynamics, this permits system-size-independent Trotter steps when estimating local observables. Combining this compression with Richardson extrapolation, we provide classical and quantum error bounds with respect to the 2-norm of the propagated observable. These give high-probability expectation-value guarantees for random input states or random Hamiltonians acting on a fixed state and control (out-of-time-order) correlators. Concretely, we show that expectation values of local observables at time $t$ can be estimated to accuracy $\varepsilon$ using circuits of maximum depth $O\!\left(\left[1+\left(t/\gamma\right)^{3/2}\right]\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\right)$, independent of the system size $n$. Classically, we show that sparse Pauli propagation runs in time polynomial in $n$, $t$ and $1/\varepsilon$ for every fixed $\gamma>0$, with polynomial degree $O(1/\gamma)$ in the weak dissipation limit. The gap between our quantum and classical upper bounds leaves room for a substantial polynomial quantum advantage as dissipation weakens, an observation further supported by our numerical results.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Strong Simulation of 1D Quantum Circuits via Reduced Transition Matrices
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Tensor networks are powerful tools for simulating quantum many-body systems, but the growth of spatial entanglement severely limits the direct evolution of pure states under chaotic unitary circuits. Here we address the task of evaluating specified output probabilities of one-dimensional circuits at finite relative precision. We introduce a sweeping algorithm that contracts the circuit transversely and compresses its two temporal boundaries jointly through reduced transition matrices (RTMs), preserving their overlap rather than either boundary separately. At fixed target precision, the retained bond dimension exhibits a slowdown consistent with subexponential growth over the accessible time window, in a regime where the circuit is already deeply anticoncentrated. A noisy random-operator model illustrates how finite precision can induce a crossover from linear to logarithmic temporal entropy growth. These results open a route to probability queries for benchmarking and learning without representing the full quantum state.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\sim\lambda/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Generative marginal learning for finite-size molecular simulation with application to stress calculation
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We propose generative marginal learning (GML), a framework for equilibrium sampling and local observable estimation in molecular simulations. By training a conditional diffusion model on large-system simulations, GML learns the marginal distribution of a retained region, enabling configuration generation without explicitly simulating the surrounding environment or imposing periodic boundary conditions on the retained region. We derive a marginal effective potential and the associated conditional mean-force identity, which provide the basis for both denoising and force-alignment training. As an application, we estimate the spatially averaged Irving--Kirkwood stress near a vacancy defect. Numerical tests on a two-dimensional Lennard--Jones crystal and three-dimensional BCC Fe under combined tension and shear demonstrate improved local stress accuracy relative to small periodic molecular dynamics simulations.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Helium States in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Inspired by Quantum Photonics
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2). We then investigate the performance of this circuit architecture as a basis for implementing the VQD method. In the ideal noiseless simulation setting, we see that the survival probability of the ground and the excited states within the target $CAS$ subspace is unity, because the total photon number and the photon number in the two spin sectors $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are preserved. We demonstrate that the proposed approach enables the determination of the ground and excited-state energies within the CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space using a continuous-variable quantum circuit and the variational quantum deflation ($VQD$) algorithm, while satisfying the orthogonality conditions with negligible errors.
